description: LLMRouter: An Open-Source Library for LLM Routing

summary.one_liner: LLMRouter is an open-source Python library and CLI for LLM routing that picks the most suitable model for each query to balance quality, cost, and latency.
summary.what_it_does: It provides over 16 router models grouped into single-round, multi-round, multimodal, personalized, and agentic categories, including KNN, SVM, MLP, matrix factorization, Elo rating, graph-based, and BERT-based methods. A unified `llmrouter` CLI supports training routers, running inference (single query, batch file, or route-only), and launching a Gradio chat interface. A data generation pipeline builds routing training data from 11 benchmark datasets by calling LLM APIs and evaluating responses. The README also describes a ComfyUI visual interface, a plugin system for custom routers and tasks, an xRouteBench benchmark pipeline, and an OpenAI-compatible OpenClaw Router server. Installation is via pip (llmrouter-lib) or editable install from source.
use_cases: route queries to the cheapest adequate LLM
train a KNN, MLP, or SVM model router on benchmark data
benchmark LLM routing strategies on xRouteBench
chat with a routed set of LLMs through a Gradio UI
deploy an OpenAI-compatible routing API server
route time series or multimodal queries to the right model
how_to_run: git clone <repo> && cd LLMRouter && conda create -n llmrouter python=3.10 && pip install -e .
llmrouter infer --router knnrouter --config config.yaml --query "What is machine learning?"
notable: Covers 16+ routing methods (KNN, SVM, MLP, MF, Elo, GraphRouter, RouterDC, AutoMix, Hybrid LLM, Router-R1) under one unified CLI and config format
Plugin system auto-discovers custom routers from ./custom_routers/ and ~/.llmrouter/plugins/
Data generation pipeline covers 11 benchmark datasets, including multimodal tasks on Geometry3K, MathVista, and Charades-Ego
OpenClaw Router exposes routing as an OpenAI-compatible API server for chat platforms
Supports local OpenAI-compatible servers such as Ollama and vLLM, and per-service API key dicts
caveats: Router-R1 installation requires a GPU and pins vllm==0.6.3 and torch==2.4.0
Inference, chat, and data generation require API keys for LLM providers unless using route-only mode
Some routers are marked training N/A (smallest_llm, largest_llm, llmmultiroundrouter), and router_r1 training is listed as LINK rather than a built-in training step
keywords: pick cheapest model for each query
